===Qwen & Hermes’ pick===

Pick from 2026-10-19 (Oct 3 weeks 2026, entries 10/19–10/24)

Score: 9/10 — core hits on Topological + Magnon + Theoretical; indirect Altermagnet (zero-net-moment compensation, the design goal the altermagnetism thread pursues); phonon/skyrmion absent (the week’s top phonon entry is the runner-up below).

Title: Magnon Chern Insulator in Two-Dimensional Fully Compensated Ferrimagnetic Heterostructures ID: PRL 137, 176601 — 10.1103/wh99-b81w Authors: Yingxi Bai, Zhiqi Chen, Baibiao Huang, Ying Dai, Chengwang Niu (Shandong Univ.) Date: 10/23 entry (PRL published 22 Oct 2026)

why this pick?

This is the topological magnon the magnon picks have been building toward. The 08/31 pick (2609.02008 chiral magnons) and the 09/07 pick (two-magnon spectroscopy in altermagnets) read out magnons that are still linear, spectroscopic modes. This paper crosses the line: it turns the magnon spectrum itself into a topological band — a magnon Chern insulator with a nonzero magnon Chern number and chiral edge magnon states, in a magnet with zero net magnetization. The mechanism is a type-III (broken-gap) band alignment: strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg exchange makes the two layers’ magnon frequency gaps non-overlapping, so the topological “gap” is the mismatch between the two single-layer gaps rather than a full bulk gap. The punchline is the transport: the asymmetric Bose–Einstein occupations of the oppositely chiral magnon branches yield a giant magnon thermal Hall conductivity that is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets — the topological charge is populated, not just present. First-principles (DFT) + Heisenberg–Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya model; experimentally accessible CrI3/CrGeTe3 and CrI3/CrSiTe3 heterostructures identified. It is the only entry this week combining genuine band topology and magnons at core, and it is the one peer-reviewed PRL in the strong candidate set — the topological sequel to your 08/31 + 09/07 magnon picks, and the cleanest demonstration that a zero-net-moment magnet (the design goal the whole altermagnetism thread chases) can still host protected magnon edge transport.

1. Keyword matching across the six interests (every line checked against the verified abstract)

Interest How this paper connects
Topological Core: realizes a magnon Chern insulator — nonzero magnon Chern numbers, chiral edge magnon states, protected by a type-III (broken-gap) band alignment.
Magnon Core: the object of study is the topological magnon spectrum — chiral magnon branches, asymmetric Bose occupations, giant magnon thermal Hall.
Theoretical Core: a general theoretical framework + Heisenberg–DM model + first-principles (DFT) identification of material platforms; no experimental input assumed.
Altermagnet Indirect: the substrate is a fully compensated ferrimagnet (zero net moment), not a collinear altermagnet — but it shares the exact design philosophy the altermagnetism program is built on (kill the stray field, keep the spin response), and the zero-net-moment compensated magnetism is the same “no stray field” end-state.
Phonon Not addressed: no ionic degrees of freedom. The week’s only strong phonon entry (2610.29453 alteraxial phonons) is the runner-up below — the altermagnet×phonon analogue of this pick’s altermagnet theme, if phonon is the priority.
Skyrmion Not addressed.

*Indirect: the paper’s framework intersects the area even if it is not the primary focus.

The runner-up 2610.29453 is the best phonon entry of the week and the most novel bridge to your altermagnetism thread — it classifies alteraxial phonons (p/d/f/g/i-wave phonon-angular-momentum textures with 1–6 zero-PAM nodal lines) and develops a nonlinear PAM-transport theory with parity + angular-harmonic selection rules, explicitly framed as “analogous to altermagnets” (d/g/i-wave momentum-dependent split). It is the pick if phonon takes priority this week. 2610.28854 and 2610.23699 are genuine skyrmion × magnon hits, but their “topological” is only via the skyrmion texture, and you already have two texture-focused picks this cycle (09/14 skyrmion stabilization, 09/21 optical readout), so they would repeat that line. 2610.30371 is the strongest altermagnet material-design entry (118 meV d-wave splitting from interfacial charge transfer + octahedral tilts) but has no magnon/topology core. 2610.25489 (circular-optical compensation in MnTe altermagnets) is the theoretical cousin of last week’s phr7-1zy5 optical-response pick — a strong companion, not a new axis. I rank wh99-b81w above all because it is the only candidate carrying topology + magnon at core (your two top interests in one paper) with a true topological invariant (magnon Chern number) and zero net magnetization, and it is the only peer-reviewed PRL in the set — the topological step-up the magnon picks have been reaching for.

3. Physical insights from this paper

  • Compensation + asymmetry = topological magnon with no stray field. Fully compensated (zero-net-moment) magnetism was assumed to suppress the Hall/thermal-Hall signatures that a net moment provides; here a strong asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg exchange across the two layers makes their magnon frequency gaps non-overlapping (type-III broken-gap alignment), producing a nonzero magnon Chern number and chiral edge magnon states in a magnet that cannot stray-field a neighbor — topology of gaps, not of a single gapped band.
  • The Bose occupation is the engine, not a spectator. It is not merely the band topology that gives the signal: the asymmetric Bose–Einstein occupations of the oppositely chiral branches are what generate the giant magnon thermal Hall, which is outright forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. So the resource is a chirally populated, two-sublattice magnon spectrum — something a single AFM layer cannot provide.
  • It is a platform, not just a model. CrI3/CrGeTe3 and CrI3/CrSiTe3 are flagged as experimentally accessible by first-principles, so the “zero-net-moment topological magnon” is a concrete heterostructure-engineering proposal (stack two different 2D magnets, tune the intralayer exchange) plus a testable magnon-thermal-Hall prediction — a falsifiable design target, in the spirit of your altermagnet picks’ material-platform line.
  • The arc completes. 08/31 (chiral magnon, linear transport, 3D chiral magnet) → 09/07 (two-magnon spectroscopy, the magnon probe) → this (topological magnon, Chern edge states, zero-net-moment compensated ferrimagnet). The magnon thread crosses from “read the magnon” to “topologically engineer the magnon” — the natural next step for a low-dissipation, stray-field-free magnon device.

TL;DR

A two-dimensional fully compensated (zero-net-moment) ferrimagnet hosts a magnon Chern insulator: an asymmetric intralayer Heisenberg exchange across the two layers creates a type-III (broken-gap) band alignment with nonzero magnon Chern numbers and chiral edge magnon states, and the asymmetric Bose–Einstein occupations of the oppositely chiral branches produce a giant magnon thermal Hall that is forbidden in conventional antiferromagnets. First-principles identifies CrI3/CrGeTe3 and CrI3/CrSiTe3 as accessible platforms — the week’s only entry combining topology + magnon at core, and the topological step-up of your 08/31 + 09/07 magnon picks. (PRL 137, 176601, 22 Oct 2026.)
